findings.issue: The example-pin check (P123.27) cannot be satisfied across a release. verify.sh --release runs it before the tag exists (`tag v$version does not exist yet` is checked in the same block), so repinning the example to the new tag in the release commit is a `tag-unavailable` refusal (exit 1) and the release preflight fails; leaving it on the previous tag passes preflight, but the moment the new tag exists `pin-behind-newest-tag` (a finding, not a refusal) fires. And the live case l1 accepts only refusals, so it goes red in the ordinary per-commit sweep - which CI runs with fetch-depth 0, tags included - on every commit after the release until a follow-up repin. CONTRIBUTING.md says the check 'belongs to the release set alone', which l1 contradicts. This lands at the imminent 3.3.0 tag.
findings.resolution: Let the release check accept a pin equal to the version being released (plugin.json's) as 'pending this release's tag' rather than tag-unavailable, so the follower can be repinned in the release commit; and drop the pin-behind arm from l1 (keep l1 to script-missing-at-tag over existing tags), or move the live claim out of the per-commit sweep.
